key_insight: A multi-domain EEG model combining spectral, connectivity, and topological features improved subject-level ADHD classification, with SVM performing best.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EEG-based machine learning may help support more objective ADHD biomarker research, though it is not ready to replace clinical assessment.
method: EEG from 121 subjects was preprocessed and split into overlapping windows for feature extraction.
Three feature domains were combined: spectral features, wPLI functional connectivity, and persistent homology topological descriptors.
RFE selected 110 features from 1,043 total descriptors; five classifiers were tested with stratified five-fold cross-validation.
evidence_signal: The best model, an SVM, achieved 80.17% accuracy, 80.95% F1-score, 80.14% balanced accuracy, 86.72% ROC-AUC, and 87.34% PR-AUC.
watch_item: Performance comes from a relatively small sample and cross-validation on a single dataset, so external validation is needed before broader use.
paper_title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
